{{Short description|German chemist (born 1946)}}
'''Siegfried Blechert''' (born 1 March 1946 in [[Aalborg]], [[Denmark]]) is a German [[chemist]].<ref name="olf">{{cite journal | last1 = Schuster | first1 = Matthias | last2 = Blechert | first2 = Siegfried | title = Die Olefinmetathese in der organischen Synthese | journal = Angewandte Chemie | volume = 109 | pages = 2124 | year = 1997 | doi = 10.1002/ange.19971091904 | issue = 19| bibcode = 1997AngCh.109.2124S }}</ref>

Blechert studied chemistry at the [[University of Hannover]], [[Germany]] and completed his [[PhD]] under the supervision of [[Ekkehard Winterfeldt]] in 1974. After a research stay with [[Pierre Potier]] in Gif-sur-Yvette, [[France]], in 1981, he finished his [[habilitation]] at the University of Hannover in 1982 and there became lecturer in [[organic chemistry]]. In 1986 he took up a professorship at the [[University of Bonn]]. In 1990 he accepted the chair of the Organic Chemistry Department at [[Technische Universität Berlin]].<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.chemie.tu-berlin.de/blechert/menue/ueber_uns/organisationleitung/curriculum_vitae/ | title = CV Siegfried Blechert}}</ref>

His research interests include the development of new catalysts for [[olefin metathesis]], novel synthetic methods, and the stereoselective synthesis of natural products.<ref name="olf"/>
